text:
Dear Teodora,

I moved out of 4B Larchfield Court, Mill Road, Cambridge CB1 2XY on 31 August and returned all three sets of keys to Kwabena Mensah the same day. Kwabena carried out the check-out inspection with me and wrote "minor wear only, no damage" on the report.

Your email of 12 September says you are keeping 380 pounds of my 1,450-pound deposit for carpet cleaning and repainting the hallway. The tenancy agreement only requires professional carpet cleaning if a pet lived in the flat, and I never kept a pet. Kwabena also told me by phone that he did not record any marks in the hallway.

Please return the full deposit, or send itemised invoices, within 14 days. The deposit is protected under scheme reference DPS-7741-0928-3. I can be reached on 07700 900418 or at j.okafor-hale@example.com.

Kind regards,
Jide Okafor-Hale
task: Make this deposit letter to my old landlord firmer but still polite, and point out exactly where her deductions contradict the check-out report and the tenancy terms.

text:
Complaint for the broadband provider, please help me tidy this up before I send it.

Account holder: Marguerite Delacroix-Bah
Account number: FBX-00458213
Service address: Flat 2, 19 Quayside Row, Bristol BS1 4ZZ
Contact: 07700 900237

Our fibre line has been down since 14 October, which is now 9 days. An engineer visit was booked for 17 October and again for 20 October, and nobody turned up either time. On the second call your agent, Dmitri, apologised and offered a 12-pound credit. I work from home three days a week and have been using mobile data, which cost me an extra 34 pounds this month. I am not asking to leave the contract yet, but I want a confirmed engineer date and compensation for every day without service, not a one-off credit. If the line is not fixed by 31 October I will escalate to the ombudsman.
task: Tidy up this broadband complaint so it reads clearly and firmly, keeping my timeline and exactly what I'm asking for.

text: Background for a message to my neighbour. Sigrún Halldórsdóttir is our next-door neighbour at 43 Ashdown Lane. The storm on Sunday blew down two panels of the shared fence. When we spoke over the hedge on Monday, Sigrún said she would "probably" pay half, but only if we used her brother-in-law's firm. Her husband, Bjarni, later texted me from 07700 900561 saying they'd rather wait until spring. The cheapest quote I have is 240 pounds for both panels plus posts, from a local fencer; the brother-in-law quoted 310 pounds. Our dog keeps getting into their garden, so I can't wait until spring. I'd like to suggest splitting the 240-pound quote 50/50 and offer to handle the booking myself. Sigrún's email is sigrun.h@example.org if that's a better channel than texting Bjarni.
task: Help me write a friendly but clear message to my neighbours proposing how we split the fence repair.

text:
Claim notes so far: water damage, kitchen

Policyholder: Nguyen Minh Chau
Policy no.: HSH-2209-77814-C
Claim ref: CLM/88/40217

On 2 February the inlet hose on our washing machine split while we were out. The kitchen laminate (about 14 square metres) has lifted and the bottom of two base units is swollen. Our plumber, Fintan Gallagher, replaced the hose the same evening and wrote that the hose failed from age, not from a fitting error.

The loss adjuster, Ms Oduya, visited on 9 February. She said the flooring and units are covered under escape of water, but the washing machine itself and the hose are not, because they count as wear and tear. My excess is 350 pounds. She thought the insurer would probably offer a cash settlement rather than send their own fitters, though she couldn't promise that.

Next step: reply to her at r.oduya@adjusters.example.
task: Draft my reply to the loss adjuster asking how a cash settlement would be calculated and how long it normally takes.

text:
Message for our flat group chat about the energy bill, need help making it clear and not passive-aggressive.

The supplier billed us 486.20 pounds for September to November, but that's based on an estimated reading. I took an actual reading on 1 December: 48,215 kWh, not 48,512 as printed on the bill, so we've been overcharged and I've asked them to reissue it. Until the corrected bill arrives, nobody should pay anything.

Splitting: Ayaan Qureshi moved in on 15 October, so he only owes for half the period, not a full third. Liesl says she'll cover Ayaan's gap for now, but only if he pays her back by the end of January. Mirela thinks the standing charge should still be split three ways for the whole quarter; I'm not sure she's right, so let's check the tenancy agreement before deciding. I'll forward the corrected bill as soon as I get it.

text:
Notes from this morning's call on PO 4500-3318 (nitrile gloves), need a correction email to the supplier.

- We ordered 400 boxes of 100, not 40. The PO went out with 40 because of a typo on our side; Halvard Eriksen on our team spotted it on Tuesday.
- Their account manager, Adaeze Nwosu, confirmed they can ship the extra 360 boxes, but only if the amended PO reaches them before 12 December.
- Size split stays the same: 50% medium, 30% large, 20% small.
- Adaeze said they might be able to deliver in two drops (half on 16 December, half in the first week of January). That's not confirmed.

task: Write a correction email to the glove supplier based on these call notes.

text:
Moved into a rented flat last month and the fibre keeps dropping. Details:

- Router: AVM Fritz!Box 7530, firmware 7.57
- Event log, roughly every 40 minutes: "PPP negotiation failed (error 651)" followed by "DSL synchronisation lost"
- Speed test just before a drop: 62 Mbps down, 18 Mbps up; the contract says "up to 80 Mbps"
- Line is VDSL2 (FTTC), so it's copper from the street cabinet

I've already swapped the microfilter, tried the test socket behind the faceplate and factory-reset the router. The drops still happen on the test socket, which I think points away from the flat's internal wiring. The letting agent says the landlord isn't responsible for the broadband line itself, only for the wall socket.

Is error 651 more likely a line fault or a router config problem? And does Ofcom's broadband speeds code of practice apply if the problem is dropouts rather than slow speeds?
task: Help me work out whether this is a line fault I should report to my provider or something I can fix myself.

  client_key: key=proc_51b9e0d7_fake
  sftp_host: sftp.harrowgate-supply.example

Log:
02:14:07 POST /api/v2/po -> 401 Unauthorized {"error":"invalid_client_key"}
02:14:09 fallback: sftp put po_batch_1103.csv -> Permission denied (publickey,password)

Both steps worked on Friday night's run, and nobody on our side has touched the config since. The failed batch is all Velmont Hospitals orders; we're under NDA with them, and their framework discount (17.5%) was applied in the file. Harrowgate's release notes mention a key rotation on 1 November. Did the rotation break both the API and the SFTP fallback, or are these two separate problems?
